question:
In a matrix laboratory activity, students select $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$. After calculating $A^2$, they notice that the matrix satisfies a relation involving $A$, the identity matrix $I$, and the zero matrix. They attempt to use this relation to obtain $A^{-1}$ without initially applying the standard inverse formula. The result is then checked using the determinant and adjoint of $A$.

(a) Calculate $A^2$.

(b) Verify that $A^2-3A+I=O$.

(c) Use the verified relation to determine $A^{-1}$.

(d) Calculate $|A|$ and $\operatorname{adj}A$ and hence verify the inverse.
explanation:
(a)
$$A^2=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
$$A^2=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 3\\3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
$$A^2-3A+I=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 3\\3 & 2\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}5-6+1 & 3-3\\3-3 & 2-3+1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0\\0 & 0\end{bmatrix}=O$$
Hence, the relation is verified.

(c)
From
$$A^2-3A+I=O$$
we obtain
$$3A-A^2=I$$
$$A(3I-A)=I$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=3I-A$$
$$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0\\0 & 3\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$

(d)
$$|A|=2(1)-1(1)=1$$
Also,
$$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
This agrees with the inverse obtained from the matrix relation.
